To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

tumor-specific immunity induced by MN-primed variants is mediated by both L3T4 and Lyt- 2 cells, and is associated with the release of high levels of IL-2, IFN-gamma, and TNF-alpha in vivo and in vitro.

1) the immunogenicity of MNNG-treated variants is related to the expression of a tumor-specific antigen, 2) tumor-specific immunity is associated with a DTH reaction, and 3) the effector cells are L3T4+.

the anti-parental tumor immune response induced by immunization with highly immunogenic variants of the L5178Y or P815 tumor cells is mediated by T cells, and is dependent on the presence of L3T4+, but not Lyt 2+, T cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new immunotherapeutic strategies for the treatment of cancer.
the development of immunotherapeutic strategies against tumors based on the immunological effects of mutagenized tumor variants.
the mechanisms involved in the generation of tumor-specific T-cell responses in mice immunized with MNNG-treated tumor variants.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the mechanisms of tumor rejection induced by MNNG- or triazene-treated tumor cells are similar, but not identical.
L3T4 and L3T4 + Lyt-2 cells are involved in the immune response against MNNG treated L5178Y cells.

the immunization with the immunogenic variants of the L5178Y or P815 cell lines, which are capable of eliciting anti-parental tumor-specific T-cell responses in vivo, is a useful model to study the mechanisms of anti-tumor immunity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

MNNG-treated L5178Y variants are capable of inducing tumor-specific immunity and protection against parental tumors in mice, which is associated with the detection of tumor-specific delayed-type hypersensitive reactions and the release of interleukin-2 (IL-2) and interferon-gamma (IFN-gamma).

the tumor-specific reactivities of T-cell subsets from immunized mice can be studied by using MNNG-treated cell variants, and that the T-cell-mediated anti-parental immunity induced by MN-NG-treated variants is mediated by both L3T4- and Lyt- 2+ lymphocytes.
tumor-specific L3T2+ and L3T4+, as well as non-specific Lyt-2- and L3T3+, lymphocytes are involved in the anti-parental tumor response induced by immunization with MNNG-treated tumor cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the tumor-specific reactivities of L3T4 and Lyt- 2 lymphocytes are not restricted to immunization with xenogenized cells, but can also be induced by immunization with mutagenized cell clones, and that these T-cell populations are involved in the induction of anti-parental immunity.
L3T4+, but not Lyt2+ lymphocytes are involved in the DTH reaction.

the immunization of mice with MNNG-treated variants of L517Y or P815 tumors induces tumor-specific T lymphocyte populations that are enriched in the L3T4 subset and that can be transferred with unfractionated spleen cells or L3T4-enriched spleen cells.
